problem_statement: When the calling thread has no message queue configured, `msg_avail()` returns a non-zero value instead of 0. This means a loop such as `while (msg_avail())` never terminates, because the function cannot distinguish "no queue" from "queue has messages." `msg_avail()` must return 0 when the calling thread has no message queue, so that a caller sees the same result whether the queue is absent or simply empty. The downstream effect is that `msg_queue_print()` should report "No messages or no message queue" rather than "No message queue" in that situation.
